We need to fix compilation errors: wrong constructors for Record.newRecord, OPTRecord, TSIG. Need to use appropriate constructors from dnsjava library version used. Let's recall dnsjava API.

Record.newRecord(Name name, int type, int dclass, long ttl, byte[] rdata) expects rdata as byte[]. For A record, there is a convenience method: ARecord(Name name, int dclass, long ttl, InetAddress address). Actually there is ARecord class. So we can create a new ARecord rather than using Record.newRecord with InetAddress.

So change aRecord = new ARecord(name, DClass.IN, 300, InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1"));

Need import ARecord.

Next, OPTRecord constructors: In dnsjava, there is OPTRecord(int payloadSize) constructor? Actually I think there is a constructor: OPTRecord(int payloadSize, int version, int flags, List<EDNSOption> options) etc. There is also default empty: new OPTRecord(); but there is also a constructor with (int payloadSize) maybe not. Let's check typical usage: new OPTRecord(4096); I recall there is a constructor: OPTRecord(int payloadSize) which sets version 0, flags 0. But compile error says no such constructor. So maybe version of dnsjava used is older where the constructor signature is OPTRecord(int payloadSize, int version, int flags, List<EDNSOption> options) or OPTRecord(int payloadSize, int version, int flags, EDNSOption...). There is also a no-arg constructor. So we can use new OPTRecord(); then set payload size via setter? Let's check API: class OPTRecord extends Record. It has fields: int payloadSize, int version, int flags, List<EDNSOption> options. There is a constructor: OPTRecord(int payloadSize, int version, int flags, List<EDNSOption> options) and also one with varargs EDNSOption. There's also a default constructor that sets payloadSize=0. So we can just use new OPTRecord(); and then maybe set payload size via setPayloadSize? There might be a method setPayloadSize(int). Not sure. Simpler: use new OPTRecord(0,0,0, (List<EDNSOption>)null) but that may cause NPE. However we just need an OPTRecord instance to be added; its fields not used for test beyond detection of "OPT". So we can use the no-arg constructor: new OPTRecord(); This compiles.

Thus replace all new OPTRecord(0) with new OPTRecord().

Next, TSIG constructors: In dnsjava, TSIG constructors: TSIG(Name name, String algorithm, byte[] key) maybe. Actually there is a class TSIG extends Record. I think there is a constructor: TSIG(Name name, int algorithm, long timeSigned, int fudge, byte[] mac, short originalID, int error, byte[] other). But compile error shows not found. So maybe newer version uses TSIG(Name name, String algorithm, byte[] key). There is also TSIG(Name name, String algorithm, SecretKey key). Let's check typical usage: TSIG tsig = new TSIG(Name.fromString("tsig.example."), "hmac-md5.sig-alg.reg.int.", keyBytes); That's typical.

Thus we need to create a TSIG with name and algorithm string and key bytes. For tests we just need a TSIG object; its verification state will be set via setTsigState. So we can create a TSIG with empty key.

So replace new TSIG(keyName, TSIG.HMAC_MD5, 0, 0, new byte[0], (short) 0, 0, null) with new TSIG(keyName, "hmac-md5", new byte[0])? Actually algorithm string may be "hmac-md5.sig-alg.reg.int." but we can use TSIG.HMAC_MD5 constant? In newer API, TSIG.HMAC_MD5 is a String constant maybe. Let's check: TSIG.HMAC_MD5 is a static final String representing algorithm name. So we can use new TSIG(keyName, TSIG.HMAC_MD5, new byte[0]);

Thus adjust.

Need import for ARecord.

Also need to adjust any other code referencing TSIG fields maybe not.

Now compile errors resolved.

Check other imports: Already have import org.xbill.DNS.*? Actually they import org.xbill.DNS.*? Not. They import only specific classes: package org.xbill.DNS; but they are in same package, so they can use classes without import. So ARecord, TSIG, OPTRecord are accessible.

Now adjust code accordingly.
